title: Is Monetarism Making a Comeback?
gist: Tim Congdon argues that monetarism, after decades on the margins of mainstream economics, is re-entering the debate — most notably at the Federal Reserve — but must learn from past mistakes and adapt to 21st-century monetary and financial realities such as fintech and global payments to regain credibility.

insights.claim: After decades on the margins of mainstream economic thinking, monetarism is beginning to re-enter the policy debate, most notably at the Federal Reserve.
insights.speaker: TIM CONGDON
insights.so_what: A revival of money-supply-focused analysis at the Fed could shift how the central bank reads inflation risk — worth tracking for anyone positioning around the reaction function for rates.
insights.quote: After decades on the margins of mainstream economic thinking, monetarism is beginning to re-enter the debate, most notably at the Federal Reserve.

insights.claim: To regain credibility, monetarists must learn from past mistakes and adapt to the monetary and financial realities of the 21st century.
insights.speaker: TIM CONGDON
insights.so_what: Signals that any monetarist comeback will be a modified doctrine, not a return to 1980s money targeting — tempering how literally to read money-supply signals.
insights.quote: monetarists must learn from past mistakes and adapt to the monetary and financial realities of the 21st century

insights.claim: The 2026 Jackson Hole symposium, hosted by the Kansas City Fed, is organized around the theme 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy,' and will almost certainly focus on the monetary-policy challenges posed by fintech and global payment systems.
insights.speaker: TIM CONGDON
entities: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City
insights.so_what: A Fed symposium centered on payments and fintech flags where policymakers see the next monetary-transmission risks — relevant to stablecoins, digital payments, and bank-disintermediation trades.
insights.quote: organized around the theme “Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy,” will almost certainly focus on the monetary-policy challenges posed by fintech and global payment systems
